justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly bullish baseline for what appears to be an asset trading near the 365 level. For the 1-day estimate of 365.5, I was essentially anchoring very close to the current price, assuming mean-reversion dominates over very short horizons and that no major scheduled catalysts were imminent. The 1-week estimate of 368 incorporates a slight upward drift, consistent with a modest positive momentum assumption or a marginally bullish macro backdrop. The 1-month estimate of 375 extends that drift further, reflecting a longer-run tendency for risk assets to trend upward over time when no major structural headwinds are present. In each case, the point estimates are relatively close to current levels because I had no strong directional signal that would justify a large departure from the prevailing price.

The confidence interval widths reflect how uncertainty compounds with time. At one day, the 90% interval of 350–381 is relatively tight because intraday and overnight volatility is bounded under normal market conditions. At one week, the interval widens to 338–398 to account for the possibility of news events, earnings surprises, or macro data releases that could shift sentiment materially. By one month, the interval of 310–440 reflects a much broader distribution of outcomes, encompassing everything from a meaningful correction driven by risk-off sentiment to a continuation rally if conditions remain supportive. The asymmetry in the monthly interval — roughly 65 points of downside versus 65 points of upside from the point estimate — reflects a roughly symmetric uncertainty distribution, though in practice tail risks can be skewed.

There are several specific risks that could push outcomes outside my stated intervals. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in macroeconomic data, an unexpected central bank policy shift toward aggressive tightening, or a geopolitical shock could drive prices well below 310 over a month. Liquidity crises or credit events — which by definition are hard to forecast — represent the most severe tail risks. On the upside, a stronger-than-expected economic soft landing, dovish central bank pivots, or a positive sentiment cascade could push prices above 440. At the very short end, even a single large institutional trade or an unexpected after-hours announcement could briefly breach the 1-day interval, though such moves would likely partially reverse. These outer-tail scenarios are genuinely possible but not my central expectation.
